patient_question: It has been 10 days since my surgery and I still have some leakage when I cough or stand up. Is this normal? How long will it last?
physician_response: Leakage is common after this surgery and usually improves over weeks to months. Keep doing your pelvic floor exercises. We will reassess at your 6 week visit.

patient_question: My lab results came back and my PSA is undetectable. Does that mean I'm cured? When is my next test?
physician_response: An undetectable PSA is a good result. We will repeat the test in 3 months and then continue to monitor.

patient_question: I've been having trouble sleeping since my diagnosis and I keep worrying about the results. Is there anything I can do?
physician_response: Anxiety is common. You can talk to your primary care doctor about sleep options. We can also refer you to our support services.

patient_question: The incision site looks a little red today and feels warm. Should I come in?
physician_response: Please send a photo through the portal. If you have fever or the redness is spreading, go to urgent care.

patient_question: Can I start driving again? It's been two weeks and I feel fine.
physician_response: You can drive once you are off narcotic pain medicine and can brake without pain.
